newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end flat to higher, slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end flat to higher, slow trade.

text.p: Argentine bonds were flat to higher late Monday as the rally from last week ran out of steam.

"The market was timidly firm but calm," said a trader at an Argentine bank. There was a brief buyer flurry in the morning in continuation of Friday's surge, but gentle profit-taking set in around noon.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 slipped $0.08 to 120.65, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/4 to 85.
Traders said this week could prove to be a slow one because of a shortage of anticipated market-moving news both locally and abroad.
Still, even if there is gradual profit-taking this week, traders and analysts estimate the market remains fundamentally firm.

"Even if the market could show a correction during this week, with the present background, we do not expect a change of the current strong tendency in the medium term. Accordingly, we consider the probable correction as a buy opportunity," said Banco Rio in an investor note.
In the money markets, call money fell to 6.50 percent from 6.85 percent.
